clue.text: Fabric mum put back in place

indicators.note: in tells us the turned word for mum goes inside the word for place

parts.note: a site is a place or location

indicators.note: put back signals that the word for mum is turned round, read right to left

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mum

explanation.surface: Someone has misplaced a piece of cloth and Mum has returned it to its proper spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Samite is a heavy silk fabric, often interwoven with gold, worn in the Middle Ages.

clue.text: Back for a while

definitions.meaning: to back someone is to support them, as a seconder does a motion
a very short time, as in 'just a moment'

explanation.surface: Someone says they will return shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: To second a proposal is to back it; a second is also a brief interval of time.

clue.text: Author making impression on couple

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another means the first sits above the second

parts.note: a mark is an impression left on a surface
twain is an old word for two, a couple

explanation.surface: A writer is making a big impression on a pair of readers.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain was the pen name of the American author Samuel Clemens, who wrote Huckleberry Finn.

clue.text: Judge seen as conscientious type?

definitions.meaning: one who tries a case in court is a judge
a person who always does their best, one who tries hard; the question mark flags the playful coinage

explanation.surface: A magistrate is regarded as a diligent sort of person.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the verb try: one who tries cases in court, and one who tries hard.

clue.text: Disciplinarian Bill keeps learner in

indicators.note: keeps means the word for bill holds the learner letter within it

parts.note: a sticker is a bill or notice stuck up on a wall
L is the learner sign on British cars driven by a learner

explanation.surface: A strict man called Bill keeps a slow pupil behind after class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but is a posted notice; the final 'in' just reinforces 'keeps'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler insists on strict observance of rules, as a disciplinarian does.

clue.text: Changing events more successfully than Canute?

definitions.text: Changing events more successfully than Canute?

parts.words: Changing events more successfully than Canute?
parts.note: King Canute famously failed to hold back the sea; altering the course of events is the metaphor that succeeds where he failed

explanation.surface: Someone altered the course of history better than the king who sat on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: Canute (Cnut), the 11th-century king of England, is said to have ordered the incoming sea to stop, which it did not.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn the tide is the idiom for reversing the course of events, literally what Canute could not do.

clue.text: Entertainers in a disco, men dancing

indicators.note: dancing suggests the letters of the following words moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: Performers at a nightclub, with men out on the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Comedians are entertainers who make audiences laugh.

clue.text: Craft that may be demonstrated by make-up artist

definitions.meaning: a craft is a vessel, here an ocean-going passenger ship

definitions.text: that may be demonstrated by make-up artist
definitions.meaning: a make-up artist shows off a pencil used to draw lines round the eyes

explanation.surface: A skill a beautician might show off at a cosmetics counter.
explanation.definitionFit: A liner is a large passenger ship, and also a cosmetic pencil for outlining the eyes or lips.

clue.text: Money paid by tenant across the Channel — someone in a gite, say

indicators.note: across means the word for the tenant's payment stretches over and round the other piece

parts.note: rent is the money a tenant pays the landlord
in old British usage a TV channel was a side, as in 'switch over to the other side'

explanation.surface: A rent payment for a French holiday let is made from England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Channel' suggests the English Channel and France, but it is a television channel, once called a 'side' in Britain. A gîte is a French holiday cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident is someone living in a place, as an occupant of a French holiday cottage is, for example.

clue.text: Room can be found to employ this French woman

definitions.text: Room can be found to employ this French woman

parts.words: Room can be found to employ this French woman
parts.note: a French woman employed to look after a room, the French word for room being part of her title

explanation.surface: There is space in the household to hire a French maid.
explanation.definitionFit: A femme de chambre is a French chambermaid, literally a woman of the bedroom.

clue.text: Soldier in hurry going round dump

indicators.note: going round means the word for hurry surrounds the word for dump

parts.note: to career is to rush along headlong
to bin something is to dump it

explanation.surface: A soldier rushes past a rubbish tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbineer is a soldier armed with a carbine, a short rifle.

clue.text: Souls with long hair sent to head of school

indicators.note: sent to means the piece for long hair is joined on to the next piece

parts.note: a mane is a long flowing head of hair

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Spirits of pupils with long hair are being sent to the headteacher.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman religion the manes were the deified souls of dead ancestors.

clue.text: Catch son leaving home

indicators.note: leaving means the letter for son departs from the word for home

parts.note: a nest is a home, especially a bird's

explanation.surface: The family catches their son as he moves out.
explanation.definitionFit: To net something is to catch it, as a fish is caught in a net.

clue.text: Novel ne'er admired may be this

definitions.text: Novel ne'er admired may be this

indicators.note: novel, as an adjective meaning new, tells us the letters of the next words take a fresh order

explanation.surface: A book nobody ever liked may end up sold off cheap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like the book itself, but it is the signal to rearrange NE'ER ADMIRED; the whole clue also describes what happens to an unpopular book.
explanation.definitionFit: Remaindered books are unsold stock sold off cheaply by the publisher, the fate of an unloved novel.

clue.text: Wouldn't allow recitation of Shakespeare?

indicators.note: a recitation is spoken out loud, so we need a word sounding like the word for Shakespeare

parts.note: Shakespeare is known as the Bard

explanation.surface: Someone refused to let an actor perform a speech from Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: If something was barred it was forbidden, so barred replaces wouldn't allow in 'they ___ it'.

clue.text: Shuffle is a modern dance

indicators.note: dance suggests the letters moving around into new positions

explanation.surface: A dance step is said to be a contemporary dance.
explanation.definitionFit: To randomise is to put in a random order, as shuffling a pack of cards does.

clue.text: Cheer up tot in depression in Scotland

indicators.note: in places the word for tot inside the Scottish valley

parts.note: a glen is a narrow Scottish valley
to tot up is to add

explanation.surface: Cheering up a small child who is feeling low in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: To gladden someone is to make them glad, to cheer them up.

clue.text: Raw drafts rewritten for Sun?

indicators.note: rewritten means the letters of the preceding words are written out again in a new order

explanation.surface: A writer redrafts rough copy for a tabloid newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun' suggests the British tabloid newspaper, but it is the star; the question mark shows the Sun is an example of a dwarf star.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sun is classed as a yellow dwarf, a small main-sequence star, so it is an example of the type.

clue.text: Profitable English publication for kids keeps on rising

indicators.note: keeps means the children's publication holds the turned word inside

parts.note: a comic is a magazine of picture strips for children

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: An English children's paper continues to grow in profits.
explanation.definitionFit: Economic can mean profitable or paying its way, as in 'an economic rent'.

clue.text: Like section that includes article relating to law

indicators.note: that includes means the first piece holds the second within it

parts.note: conic, as in conic section, describes curves cut from a cone
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A section of a document that contains a legal clause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'section' suggests part of a document, but 'Like section' is CONIC, as in the geometrical conic section.
explanation.definitionFit: Canonic relates to canon law, the body of church law, or to a rule or canon generally.

clue.text: Soldier shouts regularly when retreating before start of rout

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word shouts
retreating means the word for when goes backwards

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A soldier yells at intervals as he falls back before the army is routed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of 'shouts' (HUS); 'retreating' turns AS into SA.
explanation.definitionFit: A hussar is a light cavalry soldier, originally from Hungary.

clue.text: The man given a drink could be Isaac

parts.note: he is the pronoun for the man
a brew is a drink, especially tea or beer

explanation.surface: A man offered a drink might turn out to be called Isaac.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac, son of Abraham in the Bible, is an example of a Hebrew, one of the ancient Israelite people.

clue.text: Exhibition centre wild with witchcraft being practised?

parts.note: the NEC is the National Exhibition Centre in Birmingham
romantic can mean wild and fanciful, as of scenery or ideas

explanation.surface: A trade fair venue gets carried away by magic.
explanation.definitionFit: Necromantic describes necromancy, sorcery involving the dead, so it suits a place where black magic is practised.

clue.text: Rib sacrifice — first thing for Adam

parts.note: a cost is what must be given up, a sacrifice

indicators.note: first thing for picks the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: The rib Adam gave up was the first price paid in Eden.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Eve made from Adam's rib.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa is the anatomical Latin term for a rib.

clue.text: Country home gone over by cleaner briefly

indicators.note: gone over by means the shortened cleaner covers and surrounds the word for home
briefly means the word for cleaner loses its last letter

parts.note: a char is a British cleaning lady, short for charwoman
in means at home

explanation.surface: A house in the country has been cleaned quickly by the help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleaner' looks like a household product, but it is a char, a British cleaning woman; 'briefly' leaves CHA.
explanation.definitionFit: China is a country in East Asia.

clue.text: English quintet disowns its classical number? Shame!

indicators.note: disowns means the word for the quintet gives up the Roman numeral

parts.note: five, in English, is a quintet
V is five in Roman numerals, the classical way of writing the number

explanation.surface: An English group of five musicians renounces its classical repertoire, to cries of disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Fie is an old exclamation of disapproval, equivalent to 'for shame!'.

clue.text: African entering Trondheim, a sailor

indicators.note: entering means the answer goes into, and is found within, the words that follow

explanation.surface: A man from Africa arrives in a Norwegian port as a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Masai are a people of Kenya and Tanzania, so a Masai is an African.

clue.text: Journalists housed in very cold accommodation

indicators.note: housed in means the journalists' piece is placed inside the word for very cold

parts.note: bitter weather is very cold
eds is short for editors, the journalists in charge

explanation.surface: Reporters are put up in freezing lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: A bedsitter is a British one-room flat with bed and living space combined.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedsitter is a one-room lodging, a form of accommodation.

clue.text: Banger not cooked and lacking a smooth surface

parts.note: a banger is British slang for an old car, also called a crate
raw meat that is not cooked is still red

explanation.surface: A sausage left uncooked looks lumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banger' suggests a British sausage, but it is an old car (CRATE).
explanation.definitionFit: A cratered surface is pitted with hollows, so it is far from smooth.

clue.text: School hospital located by sign showing direction

indicators.note: located by means the first piece sits beside the next one

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital on road signs
an arrow is a sign pointing the way

explanation.surface: A school sits next to a hospital, signposted with an arrow.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is a famous English public (private boarding) school in north-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Harrow is a well-known English independent school, the alma mater of Churchill.
